players.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
players.note: Top waiver target in this league because he is actually available and still owns a valuable Jacksonville role. Week 2 was modest (3 catches on 8 targets for 40 yards), but he appeared healthy after the shoulder issue and remained ahead of Jakobi Meyers in the pecking order. Treat as a talent/role buy-low rather than a box-score chase.

players.name: Jonah Coleman
players.note: Priority upside RB. RJ Harvey missed Week 2 and J.K. Dobbins left with a hamstring issue; Coleman responded with 10 carries for 39 yards and a TD plus 3 catches for 19 yards. Even if both veterans return, he earned a case for a larger role; if either misses time, the path to meaningful touches is immediate.

players.name: Denzel Boston
players.note: The role strengthened in Week 2 rather than fading. Boston remained Cleveland's top wideout by playing time and followed 2-59-1 in Week 1 with 5-95-1 on 7 targets. This is now a two-week role-and-production signal, not a one-game fluke.

players.name: Devaughn Vele
players.note: Week 2 confirmed the Week 1 role: 5 catches on 7 targets for 64 yards after opening 7-69-1 on 9 targets. He remains a high-participation receiver in a pass-heavy Saints offense, though Jordyn Tyson's eventual return limits the long-term ceiling.

players.name: Kaelon Black
players.note: Still a premium contingency back with some standalone work, but reduce the Week 1 excitement slightly: his 43.8% opening-week snap share was unusually high next to a healthy Christian McCaffrey, yet McCaffrey can still dominate touches in individual games. Hold rather than churn; upside remains asymmetric.

players.name: Rashod Bateman
players.note: With Zay Flowers sidelined, Bateman converted 9 targets into 7 catches, 88 yards and a touchdown. The value is tied to Flowers' availability, so treat him as a strong short-term claim rather than a permanent WR1 bet.

players.name: Emanuel Wilson
players.note: Especially relevant to this roster because Jadarian Price left Week 2 with a chest injury. Wilson handled 21 carries for 92 yards after Price exited. Negative X-rays are encouraging for Price, but Wilson is the direct hedge and should rise sharply if Price misses practice or a game.

players.name: Adonai Mitchell
players.note: Volume is forcing a re-evaluation: 12 targets in Week 2 produced 6 catches for 63 yards after a 60-yard opener. The efficiency is not elite yet, but double-digit targets create real waiver value.

players.name: Dontayvion Wicks
players.note: NFL.com's Week 3 waiver board places Wicks among the priority receiver adds. Treat as a role-growth bet that deserves a claim when the roster can use WR upside, but below the strongest two-week breakouts.

players.name: Tre Tucker
players.note: Week 2 delivered 5 catches on 7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown. Worth monitoring/adding where available, but the profile still needs another week of target stability before jumping the stronger role-based breakouts.

players.name: Keon Coleman
players.note: Caught all 6 targets for 63 yards as DJ Moore dealt with an AC-joint injury. Useful contingent value, but the ceiling depends on Moore's status and whether the target bump persists.

players.name: Tank Bigsby
players.note: Saw 13 carries for 33 yards and a TD plus two catches after Saquon Barkley suffered a stinger. Valuable contingency role, but monitor Barkley's health before spending a premium claim.

players.name: Dalton Schultz
players.note: Massive Week 2 volume (14 targets, 12 catches, 140 yards) follows 8 targets in Week 1. Strong TE pickup in a vacuum, but this roster already has Dalton Kincaid, so do not overpay unless Kincaid's role or health changes.

players.name: Tyler Shough
players.note: Through two weeks he has 90 pass attempts, 7.4 yards per attempt and 13 rushes, with consecutive useful fantasy performances. That is a meaningful breakout profile, but Jalen Hurts makes QB waiver spending unnecessary for this roster.

players.name: Bryce Young
players.note: Back-to-back strong fantasy outputs with three passing touchdowns in each of the first two weeks. Useful in QB-needy leagues, but not a roster priority behind Hurts.

players.name: Kaleb Johnson
players.note: Week 2 brought 8 carries for 32 yards and a workload competitive with MarShawn Lloyd. Worth a bench watch where available, but not yet enough role certainty for a premium claim.

players.name: Malik Washington
players.note: Has 13 targets through two games and could gain short-term opportunity if Caleb Douglas' ankle limits him. More of a contingent add than a core claim.

players.name: Caleb Douglas
players.note: The underlying role remains attractive (51 of 56 snaps and 26 routes on 30 dropbacks in Week 2), but he left with an ankle injury and was seen in a walking boot after only 2 catches for 19 yards. Downgrade from last week's STRONG claim until practice status improves.

players.name: Alvin Kamara
players.note: Remove last week's harsh downgrade. Kamara returned in Week 2 and out-touched Travis Etienne 14-10. Efficiency was poor, but the workload shows he still belongs in the mix. Treat as a watch/bench value rather than an avoid.

players.name: RJ Harvey
players.note: Hamstring injury kept him out of Week 2 after limited practices. Do not let an OUT tag automatically turn him into an IR-stash priority: Jonah Coleman performed well in his absence and could keep a larger role. Verify practice participation and ESPN IR eligibility before acting.
